title: Effects of polar quercetin and non-polar resveratrol on the functional properties, oxidative stability and interfacial behavior of camellia oil body emulsions.
abstract: This study investigated the effects of quercetin and resveratrol on the functional properties, oxidative stability, and interfacial behavior of camellia oil body emulsions. Polyphenols were incorporated individually and in combination to examine their interactions with interfacial proteins and the lipid phase. Quercetin preferentially interacted with OB surface proteins via hydrogen bonding, lowering interfacial tension from 18 to 14 mN/m and increasing hydrophobicity, while resveratrol mainly stabilized the lipid phase. Their combination significantly enhanced the thermal stability, interfacial protein concentration, and droplet stability, as confirmed by Turbiscan analysis. Polyphenol incorporation markedly suppressed lipid oxidation, reducing PV from 60 ± 4 to 22 ± 2 meq/kg and improving DPPH and ABTS radical scavenging capacities up to 70 %, with OB-QR showing the highest antioxidant performance. FTIR revealed protein conformational changes, and decreased sulfhydryl and amino groups indicated polyphenol-protein interactions. Overall, polarity-driven partitioning enabled dual-phase stabilization, offering a clean-label strategy for OB-based formulations.
